questions.q: What is the core idea behind defense in depth?
options: Stacking multiple independent security layers so no single control's failure compromises the whole system
Relying entirely on employee training with no technical controls
Buying the most expensive single firewall available and relying on it exclusively
Disabling monitoring once a firewall and antivirus are in place
questions.explain: Defense in depth assumes every control eventually fails, so layers are stacked so an attacker still has to get through several independent ones.

questions.q: In the layered model, what does network segmentation (VLANs) primarily limit?
options: The number of employees who can use email
How far an attacker can move laterally once a device inside the network is compromised
Which antivirus signatures are installed
The speed of the internet connection
questions.explain: Segmentation keeps a compromised device on one zone from directly reaching sensitive systems on another zone.

questions.q: In the phishing example, why does least privilege limit the damage even after a malicious file partially executes?
options: Because the compromised account never had more access than it actually needed, like domain admin rights
Because least privilege automatically deletes malware
Because least privilege blocks all outbound internet traffic
Because least privilege replaces the need for a firewall
questions.explain: Least privilege means a compromised account can't reach everything, because it was never granted more access than its normal job required.

questions.q: Why isn't buying ten firewalls considered real defense in depth?
options: Because it's one layer repeated, with the same blind spot, rather than independent layers that fail for different reasons
Because defense in depth only applies to endpoint protection
Because having more than one firewall is against industry standards
Because firewalls are never an effective security control
questions.explain: True defense in depth requires independence of failure — layers whose weaknesses aren't the same weakness repeated.

questions.q: What role does monitoring and logging play in the layered model?
options: It replaces the need for a perimeter firewall
It's the detection layer underneath everything else, catching what every preventive layer missed
It only matters before an incident happens, not after
It is optional once endpoint protection is installed
questions.explain: Monitoring and logging act as a safety net, catching activity that got past every preventive layer above it.
